blocking_issues: Compliance: no wording that the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements (compliance-checklist, Legal and travel information). Fixed by the first edit, an exact one-paragraph replacement.

edits.location: Closing H2 'Get the legal side settled before you book', paragraph 3 (final disclaimer)
edits.issue: BLOCKING (compliance-checklist, Legal and travel information): no wording says the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. The close only says it is not legal advice.
edits.fix: Replace the paragraph with: "This guide summarises official Australian and Italian guidance as at October 2026. Requirements change, so your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for your dates before you book. It is not legal advice; for your own circumstances, speak with a family lawyer."

edits.location: H2 'How to prove your Italian marriage back home', H3 'Apostille from the Prefettura', paragraph 1
edits.issue: Accuracy (fact_17): the source says the apostille does not expire but the underlying document may have its own validity period. 'so one is enough' drops that caveat.
edits.fix: Replace "It does not expire, so one is enough. <!-- fact_17 -->" with "The apostille itself does not expire, though the certificate it is attached to may have its own validity period. <!-- fact_17 -->"

edits.issue: Accuracy: validity comes from Italian law and recognition from s 88D, not s 88D alone; and 'which is what the Passport Office means' attributes an interpretation to the agency that fact_21 does not state.
edits.fix: Replace the paragraph with: "The apostille does not make your marriage valid or recognised; Italian law and s 88D do that. It authenticates the certificate as a genuine Italian public document. It is the Hague Convention form of legalisation, and the Passport Office says foreign certificates must be legalised. <!-- fact_17 --> <!-- fact_21 -->"

edits.issue: Advisor claim not in brand-facts.md ('confirms the appointment in writing'). Keep the not-published line, make the Advisor line an invitation, not a service claim.
edits.fix: Replace with: "Not published: Prefettura processing times. Ask your Wedded Advisor to build the appointment into your plan before you book flights home."

edits.location: H2 'Do you need to register an Italian marriage in Australia?', H3 'Make sure it is registered in Italy', paragraphs 1 and 2
edits.issue: Accuracy and generalisation: fact_13 is one comune's page (Bagno a Ripoli) and fact_14 another (Gossolengo); the draft states them as the rule everywhere. fact_14 also says the act must be SENT to the registrar within 5 days, not that it must 'reach' it.
edits.fix: Replace "For a civil wedding, the comune's registrar transcribes..." sentence with: "For a civil wedding, comune pages such as Bagno a Ripoli's (Florence) explain that the registrar transcribes the act into the civil registers after the ceremony and issues the certificate or extract. <!-- fact_13 -->" Replace "It must reach the civil registrar within 5 days, and civil effect then runs from the day of the ceremony. <!-- fact_14 -->" with "The Comune di Gossolengo explains that the signed act must be sent to the civil registrar within 5 days, and civil effect then runs from the day of the ceremony. <!-- fact_14 -->"

edits.location: H2 'The legal test', H3 'When an Italian marriage would not be recognised', paragraph after the list
edits.issue: Accuracy (fact_07, s 23B(1)(d)(iii)): the ground is not understanding the 'nature and effect' of the ceremony; the draft says only 'its effect'.
edits.fix: Replace "or who did not understand its effect." with "or who did not understand the nature and effect of the ceremony."

edits.issue: Precision: the 'valid where it took place' limb comes from s 88C (Part VA applies) and the recognition rule and exceptions from s 88D, so 'the test set by section 88D' is slightly narrow.
edits.fix: Replace "the test set by section 88D of the Marriage Act 1961." with "the test set by Part VA of the Marriage Act 1961." and add <!-- fact_04 --> to the markers.

edits.issue: Precision: AGD says 'generally recognised if'; 'is recognised here if' reads as a guarantee.
edits.fix: Replace "an overseas marriage is recognised here if it was valid" with "an overseas marriage is generally recognised here if it was valid"

edits.location: H2 'How to prove your Italian marriage back home', paragraph 1
edits.issue: Originality scan: 12 consecutive words match Smartraveller verbatim without attribution ('a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage'). Official source, not a competitor, so not blocking; attribute it.
edits.fix: Replace "A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage. <!-- fact_25 -->" with "Smartraveller says a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage. <!-- fact_25 -->"

edits.location: H3 'When you need a NAATI translation', paragraph 1, last sentence
edits.issue: Generalisation: fact_24 is Home Affairs guidance for visa and citizenship applications, not for every use.
edits.fix: Replace "Home Affairs asks for the original and translation together. <!-- fact_24 -->" with "For visas and citizenship, Home Affairs asks for the original and the translation together. <!-- fact_24 -->"

edits.location: H3 'Which proof suits which purpose', table row 'Visas and citizenship'
edits.issue: Generalisation (fact_24): NAATI accreditation applies to translators in Australia; translations made overseas follow the visa page's own rules.
edits.fix: Replace the cell with: "The original plus an English translation, by a NAATI-accredited translator if done in Australia <!-- fact_24 -->"

edits.location: H3 'Which proof suits which purpose', table, new row after 'Passport in a new surname'
edits.issue: Brief fit: the brief's must-include names Services Australia in the proof table, and fact_23 supports a row. Its position on an Italian certificate is not published (no marker, per qa-gates). Medicare stays out: not checked, and the article makes no claim about it.
edits.fix: Insert row: "| Centrelink (Services Australia) | Its name-change page lists an Australian marriage certificate, or original Home Affairs evidence if you changed your name overseas; whether it accepts an apostilled Italian certificate is not published <!-- fact_23 --> |"

edits.location: H2 'Changing your surname', H3 'Other states and territories', table row 'Queensland'
edits.issue: Accuracy (fact_29): 'You may not take' reads as a prohibition; the registry says you 'may not be able to take' the name automatically.
edits.fix: Replace "You may not take your partner's name automatically" with "You may not be able to take your partner's name automatically"

edits.location: H3 'Travel in the name on your passport', last sentence
edits.issue: Generalisation: 'apply to your registry once home' is not true for every state (SA and Tasmania say ask each authority or business; NT not published).
edits.fix: Replace "Book the honeymoon in your current names and apply to your registry once home." with "Book the honeymoon in your current names and sort out the name change once home."

edits.location: FAQ 'Can you use an Italian marriage certificate to change your name in Australia?'
edits.issue: Accuracy (fact_25): Smartraveller says 'usually accepted as proof', not that it proves the marriage outright.
edits.fix: Replace "It proves the marriage but may not work for a name change." with "It is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not work for a name change."

edits.location: FAQ 'Is a symbolic wedding in Italy legally binding?'
edits.issue: Precision: 'valid under Italian law, which means one the comune records' equates validity with recording. Use the source pack's suggested framing (faq_support note).
edits.fix: Replace "Australia only recognises a marriage that was valid under Italian law, which means one the comune records." with "Australia only recognises a marriage that was valid under Italian law, and a symbolic ceremony is not registered by the comune as a marriage."

edits.location: H3 'What a symbolic Italian ceremony means legally', last sentence
edits.issue: Precision: 'no Italian paperwork' is broader than the source supports (venues may still need their own permits); the point is no marriage paperwork.
edits.fix: Replace "no Italian paperwork," with "no Italian marriage paperwork,"
